- Termination for convenience: we'd like the ability to terminate the Order Form for convenience with a pro-rata refund of pre-paid committed capacity for unused months.

- Data & export: if we terminate, we need guaranteed exported KV cache and logs within 30 days and a statement on retention.

Soojin / Laura — quick legal take before we draft formal redlines:

1) General approach: For orders with material committed discounts / reserved capacity (i.e., any TCV > $150k or committed GPU capacity), we should not give an unrestricted termination-for-convenience right that simply returns cash without an exit adjustment. This undermines our capacity planning.

2) Notice window: 60 days is a reasonable compromise for committed deals. For non-committed (pay-as-you-go) customers, a 30-day opt-out is fine.

3) Exit adjustment: propose formula-based adjustment rather than open %:
   - Remaining committed fees x 0.25 for first 6 months remaining, decreasing to 0.15 for months 7–12, and pro-rata thereafter.
   - Alternatively, allow customer to choose pro-rata refund of prepayments in exchange for a reduction of future support/migration assistance from Redwood.

4) Auto-renew: keep annual auto-renew for order forms tied to committed discounts. Require opt-out notice at least 60 days prior to renewal. Allow a one-time exception for pilots to fall into a shorter notice window, but only for orders < $50k TCV.

5) Data export: commit to export within 30 days for user data and embeddings; for full KV/operational caches we can commit to 45 days and offer an optional paid export assist.

If you want, I can draft specific MSA and Order Form redline language this morning. Need confirmation on the TCV thresholds from Finance (Laura).

— Karthik
Associate General Counsel | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>

Date: 2027-04-29 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: Termination for Convenience and Refunds

Jane — thanks for the patience. We discussed internally and here’s a targeted counterproposal that balances ACME’s flexibility with predictable economics for reserved capacity:

1) Termination for Convenience (Order Form): ACME may terminate an Order Form for convenience by giving Redwood at least 60 days’ written notice. If terminated mid-term for an Order Form with committed capacity, Redwood will:
   a) Refund any pre-paid, unused portion of fees on a pro-rata basis for the remainder of the then-current term, less an early-termination adjustment equal to 15% of the remaining committed fees (applies to orders with TCV >= $150,000).
   b) For orders with TCV between $50,000 and $149,999, early-termination adjustment will be 10%. Orders under $50,000 receive pro-rata refund with no adjustment.

2) Auto-Renew: Order Forms will renew automatically for successive 12-month periods unless ACME provides written notice of non-renewal at least 60 days prior to the end of the then-current term. Pilot orders (< $50k TCV) may elect a 30-day opt-out by ticking a checkbox on the Order Form.

3) Data Export & Retention: Redwood will provide a full export of customer data and model outputs within 30 days of an effective termination date. For KV caches and large operational artifacts, Redwood will provide export within 45 days or offer a paid export-assist service to expedite delivery.

4) Optional: If ACME prefers service credits instead of cash refunds, we can accommodate credits equal to the refund amount (net of the termination adjustment).

I have attached a redline to the MSA/Order Form reflecting the above. If this is acceptable in principle, Karthik can convert the language into final legal redlines and we’ll route to DocuSign.

Best,

— Soojin Lee
